name: Isaac Hayes
hook: A Stax songwriter and session player who turned solo albums into long, orchestral soul monologues, and became one of the most sampled voices in hip-hop.
blurb: Isaac Hayes joined Memphis's Stax Records as a session musician, and by 1964 he and David Porter were writing hits for Sam & Dave, including 'Soul Man' and 'Hold On, I'm Comin''. His own 1969 album 'Hot Buttered Soul' stretched songs into long, orchestral, string-heavy pieces with spoken introductions, and changed what a solo soul album could sound like. His 1971 'Theme from Shaft' made him the first Black composer to win the Academy Award for Best Original Song. His records' dense strings, isolated pieces of vocal and spoken interludes have made him one of the most sampled artists in hip-hop.
